news.title: Democrat Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat, becomes state’s first Black senator since 1874
news.text:
WASHINGTON: Democratic challenger Scott Colom defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in ​the Mississippi election for the US Senate, media projected on Wednesday, making him the Southern state’s first Black senator since the Reconstruction era that followed the US Civil War.

The result was a stunning upset in the heavily Republican state and expanded on the national drubbing the Democrats delivered to President Donald Trump’s Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections.

The Mississippi Senate race was one of the final races to be called after the elections. The contest was so tight that Colom at times led the vote count by only a few dozen votes.

The latest media-tabulated results showed him ahead by more than 4,500 votes, or 0.5 percentage point.

Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney, became the ‌first Democrat to win ‌a Mississippi Senate seat since John Stennis in 1982. He harnessed frustration ​over ‌the ⁠cost of ​living ⁠with a breakout campaign ad in which voters ridiculed Hyde-Smith’s suggestion that consumers could choose other “proteins” instead of paying rising beef prices.

Hyde-Smith, 67, who was appointed to the Senate in 2018 and won a special election later that year, had consistently led opinion polls in a state that Trump won by nearly 23 points in 2024. Trump campaigned in Mississippi for Hyde-Smith near the end of the race.

“While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters. I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well,” Hyde-Smith said in a video posted on ⁠social media.

Democrats’ margin grows in congress

In the midterms, Republicans lost control of ‌both chambers, leaving Trump facing a Democratic-controlled Congress for the first time in ‌either of his two terms and presenting the opposition party with a ​chance to block highly partisan legislation and investigate Trump’s ‌administration.

The Mississippi victory gives the Democrats a 55-44 advantage in the 100-member Senate, with the winner in one Senate ‌race from last week’s election — in Alaska — yet to be determined. The Democrats have also gained 41 seats in the House of Representatives so far, holding an advantage of 254 to 168 with 13 races yet to be called.

In addition, Democrats won several high-profile federal and statewide races in states long dominated by Republicans, including Texas.

Mississippi’s white voters, deep in the once-segregated South, turned ‌the state solidly Republican with the political realignment that followed the civil rights movement of the 1960s. Many of the movement’s defining battles took place in Mississippi, where ⁠Black people faced discrimination ⁠in voting, employment, education and public accommodations.

’We are on the rise’

Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, a Democrat and possible 2028 presidential contender, hailed Colom’s victory as history-making. “For too long, Southern Democrats have been overlooked, left out, and even looked down upon — but we are on the rise,” he said on X.

Colom told Reuters in an October interview that Mississippi voters felt betrayed by Trump policies such as the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices.

On the campaign trail, Colom said, he focused on reaching voters through town halls as well as visits to public housing, festivals and food trucks. “We did it the hard way, the grassroots way,” he said.

October rallies with Democratic Senators Raphael Warnock of Georgia and Cory Booker of New Jersey boosted his campaign.

The last Black candidate elected to the Senate in Mississippi was former slave Blanche Bruce in 1874.

In 2023, Hyde-Smith blocked Colom’s nomination by former President Joe Biden to ​serve as a federal district judge in northern Mississippi, ​citing his position on transgender issues. Mississippi’s other US senator, Republican Roger Wicker, supported his nomination for the post.
news.summary: Democratic challenger Scott Colom has won the Mississippi Senate seat, defeating incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith and becoming the state's first Black senator since 1874. This victory marks a significant upset in a heavily Republican state, contributing to a broader Democratic success in the recent midterm elections.
news.author: Reuters

news.title: Nvidia board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after alleged affairs
news.text:
The Nvidia board is reportedly planning to oust CEO Jensen Huang amid reports he engaged in two extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman and alleged spy and another with an executive at his tech company.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang's future with the technology giant he founded.

ABC News has reached out to Nvidia for comment.

On Sunday, Nvidia said that its board launched an independent investigation "in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."

The development on Wednesday comes after The New York Times reported nearly two weeks ago that Huang had "a close relationship" with an alleged Chinese government agent, identified as Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed. He later admitted in an internal statement to Nvidia staff that he had been "unfaithful to his wife."

Amid the fallout from the allegations and the letter, The Times reported on Wednesday that Huang also allegedly had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive who allegedly reports to him.

The outlet, citing sources within the company, reported that Huang and his colleague were allegedly captured on video being affectionate at a hotel during an Nvidia conference in March. The New York Times said it had not seen the video.

ABC News has not been able to verify the reporting or the alleged video.

Following the reporting about Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who are not related, the Chinese government denied the allegations, calling them "baseless and purely slanderous smears against China."

Neither Alice Huang nor her employer, Megaspeed International, responded to ABC News' request for comment after the New York Times story broke.

"Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected" and are part of Jensen Huang's job, an Nvidia spokesperson told ABC News at the time.

On Sunday, Nvidia shared with ABC News the internal message Jensen Huang sent to employees, in which he said he was "unfaithful," apologizing for hurting his wife and family.

"My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," the message said, in part. It did not name Alice Huang nor any other person.

Addressing Nvidia staff, partners and shareholders, Huang went on to say, "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."

"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," Huang's message said.

Following the New York Times report, congressional Republicans on the Select Committee on China sent a letter to Jensen Huang requesting that he appear for a closed-door briefing Nov. 18 concerning his relationship with Alice Huang.

The Republican chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Rep. Brian Mast, told ABC News on Tuesday that he's prepared to subpoena Huang if he does not respond by Wednesday to a request from several House Republicans.

President Donald Trump told reporters Monday that he spoke with Huang that day about the allegations.

"I asked him that question -- 'Did you have any idea that she was a spy?' He said, 'I had no idea that she was a spy,' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.

In its statement on Sunday, Nvidia said that a "committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."

Huang "fully supports the review" and will cooperate with it, the Nvidia statement further said.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," according to the statement.

"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the statement further said.

"The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team," according to the statement.

Nvidia has grown to be one of the most important chip makers in recent years due to its components being key to AI computing servers.
news.summary: The Nvidia board is reportedly planning to oust CEO Jensen Huang amid reports he engaged in two extramarital affairs.
news.author: Ivan Pereira

news.title: Nvidia 'prepares to oust' CEO Jensen Huang as he's 'caught in another scandal'
news.text: The board of one of the world's biggest artificial intelligence companies is preparing to sack its chief executive, according to reports. Nvidia boss Jensen Huang has been put into the spotlight after two alleged extramarital affairs that may have jeopardised the multi-trillion-dollar company. Mr Huang's departure would end an era in which he stoked the global AI boom, but was also riddled with scandal over his alleged affairs: one with a suspected Chinese spy and another alleged to be with an employee . The 63-year-old AI boss confessed in a memo to his staff on Sunday to carrying out an affair with a Chinese entrepreneur. She had been under investigation for allegedly passing information to Beijing. The board was planning to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine his future . Mr Huang co-founded the chipmaker in April 1993 and oversaw its rise as one of the most valuable companies in the world. He has been praised by US President Donald Trump for his work on "superintelligence". Five people who worked at the chipmaker have told the New York Time s that Mr Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, 48, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare. The alleged affair would have violated the company's code of conduct. After reports broke, Nvidia's shares ⁠plunged about eight percent in after-hours trading. The stock has lost more than $300 billion in market value since news of the affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang broke, The Mail reports. Nvidia's board had already launched an investigation into Mr Huang's affair with the alleged Chinese spy, Megaspeed founder Alice Huang. It is unclear when the two struck up a relationship, but reports detail how she would boast about how close they were as early as June 2024. In early 2025, Ms Huang pitched an AI chips deal to Chinese-based investors, touting her ability to secure Nvidia's graphics processing units and her commercial relationship with Alibaba. She had sought their investment for a southeast Asia data centre project worth several hundred million dollars, but did not disclose her relationship with Mr Huang. In the US, meanwhile, officials were briefed that Ms Huang was working for Beijing's Ministry of State Security as part of an effort to learn about American-made AI chips and possibly persuade Nvidia to make its most sophisticated semiconductors available in China , according to The New York Times . The US officials noted that the Megaspeed founder speaks English well and has relationships with executives at the highest levels of the AI chip industry. Separately, Washington was investigating Megaspeed over concerns it may have been involved in smuggling hardware to China – prompting the government to ask Nvidia to audit the firm last year. In its initial report, the chipmaker said the hardware was fully accounted for, but records obtained by Bloomberg News show that Megaspeed had imported 50,000 more chips than Nvidia found in its data centres. Nvidia then pledged in December 2025 to visit Megaspeed's data centres again, It is not clear whether this occurred.. Amid the scandal, both Nvidia and Mr Huang were sued on Monday by shareholders. The action accused the defendants of misleading shareholders about the affair before it caused Nvidia shares to dip 4.3 percent by close on Monday, reducing the company's market capitalization by approximately $190 billion.
news.summary: Jensen Huang had co-founded the chipmaker in April 1993 and oversaw its rise as one of the most valuable companies in the world. He has been praised by US President Donald Trump for his work on "superintelligence".
